title: Fpqc descent of compatible open subschemes
statement: Let $\{g_i:T_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. For each $i$, let $W_i\subset T_i$ be an open subscheme. If the pullbacks of $W_i$ and $W_j$ to $T_i\times_S T_j$ are equal for all $i,j$, then there is a unique open subscheme $W\subset S$ whose pullback to every $T_i$ is $W_i$.

proof.text: By the fibre-product point description [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points], the compatibility equalities imply that the union $W=$\bigcup_i g_i(W_i)$ is a well-defined subset of $S$ and that $g_i^{-1}(W)=W_i$ for every $i$; uniqueness of such a subset follows from the fpqc family being jointly surjective.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03N0 proof, first paragraph, using Descent Lemma Tag 02KI

proof.text: Openness of $W$ is local on the target, so fix an affine open $U$ and replace the family and the opens by their restrictions over $U$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03N0 proof, second paragraph: work Zariski locally on the base

proof.text: The affine fpqc refinement statement [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-affine-standard-refinement] supplies a finite standard fpqc family refining the restricted family. Pulling back the equality $g_i^{-1}(W)=W_i$ along the refinement gives an open inverse image in each refinement member.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03N0 proof, affine reduction and choice of a standard fpqc covering refining the given family

proof.text: Apply the standard-fpqc quotient-topology statement [lem-weil-pbc-standard-fpqc-quotient-topology] to conclude that $W$ is open on the affine neighborhood $U$. Since this holds on every affine open $U$, $W$ is open in $S$ and hence defines an open subscheme.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03N0 proof, final paragraph, applying Morphisms Lemma Tag 02JY

proof.text: The descended open subscheme is unique because its underlying open subset is uniquely determined by the equalities $g_i^{-1}(W)=W_i$, and an open subscheme is determined by its open subset with the restricted structure sheaf.
